cand.title: Canadian Infrastructure Leadership Academy 2027
cand.organizationName: Infrastructure Institute and Rotman School of Management
cand.excerpt: Verified date and venue plus credible organized-demand mechanism; venue commitments reduce current accessibility.
cand.ledgerVenue: Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto (modules Apr 14–16, Jun 16–18, Oct 27–29)

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two verified program relationship contacts: Matti Siemiatycki, CILA program co-lead and Director of the Infrastructure Institute; Geoffrey Leonardelli, CILA program co-lead and Rotman Professor of Organizational Behaviour and Human Resource Management. Both can plausibly introduce the program operations/housing decision-maker; neither is publicly identified as a hotel-contract signatory or accommodation buyer. Publicly listed institutional emails are provided in organizerContactCandidates. General operational routing is executiveprograms@rotman.utoronto.ca; the Institute also publishes infrastructure@utoronto.ca for CILA questions.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced 2027 inaugural cohort, within the requested horizon. Rotman publishes an in-person evening launch on April 13, 2027, followed by modules April 14–16, June 16–18 and October 27–29, 2027. Therefore the full activity span begins April 13, not April 14 as in the seed. These are separated attendance windows, not continuous April–October hotel demand. Monthly online sessions and flexible mentorship do not establish Toronto room nights. No subsequent 2028 edition or dates were found in the reviewed official material.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: a cohort advertised as only 30 places is not too large for the 157-room Radisson Blu Toronto Downtown, but it is a modest lodging prospect, not a 157-room buyout or a 15–109 peak-room commitment. Out-of-town delegates, faculty or speakers could generate lodging over the three module windows; actual enrollment, traveler share and nights are unpublished. Do not convert 30 seats into 30 peak rooms. The program’s city-campus delivery favors Toronto lodging over a resort; however the Harbourfront hotel is not the campus venue and would involve a campus commute. Meeting relocation is not evidenced. Optional small gatherings are a proposal only, contingent on organizer interest and verification of the hotel’s restaurant/lounge and catering operations.
findings.venueCommitments: All three in-person modules are officially assigned to Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. This is Toronto proper, in the downtown St. George campus area, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. Rotman Executive Programs publishes 105 St. George Street as its operating location and says it now only operates there; the CILA edition page does not specify a street address, classroom or launch-reception room. Treat Rotman as the published institutional venue, not a verified classroom-level or signed-contract commitment. The Infrastructure Institute footer address at 55 St. George Street is not the published CILA teaching venue.
findings.historicalRotation: The organizer describes 2027 as the inaugural cohort. No prior CILA edition, host-hotel history or destination-rotation sequence is established. The three 2027 modules are components of one cohort, not three editions. No verified annual recurrence or 2028 host commitment was located.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Edition-specific housing arrangements remain unknown: no CILA housing bureau, contracted host hotel, room block, open hotel RFP, inclusion of lodging in tuition or booking instructions were published in the reviewed CILA pages. The Institute calls the modules "three-day residential experiences"; that wording does not identify accommodation. Rotman’s general Executive Programs page states: "The hotels listed below offer a discounted rate for Rotman Executive Programs participants. Please refer to the welcome package you received for discount codes." Every listed hotel is: Kimpton Saint George; Yorkville Royal Sonesta; Double Tree by Hilton, 108 Chestnut Street; Chelsea Hotel Toronto. This establishes a general discount-code pathway, not a 2027 CILA booking commitment, allotment, exclusivity or open inventory. Whether CILA participants receive that same pathway must be confirmed.
findings.organizationStructure: A university executive-education partnership between Rotman School of Management and the Infrastructure Institute at the University of Toronto’s School of Cities, not an association convention or commercial PCO-owned event. It serves both public- and private-sector infrastructure leaders, so the government/public-sector segment is not exclusive. Rotman reviews applications through its admissions committee and awards the certificate. Future of Infrastructure Group is identified as a program-design contributor; that does not establish hotel procurement authority. No appointed PCO, DMC or housing bureau was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Rotman’s general discount list already presents four alternatives: Kimpton Saint George, Yorkville Royal Sonesta, Double Tree by Hilton and Chelsea Hotel Toronto. The first two have published Bloor Street addresses, while Executive Programs operates on St. George Street; campus convenience is therefore a plausible competitive consideration, not a measured travel-time comparison. No CILA-specific incumbent hotel, sold-out block, shortage, overflow demand or exclusive housing arrangement is evidenced. Do not describe Radisson as confirmed overflow.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Rotman Executive Programs at executiveprograms@rotman.utoronto.ca, with an introduction request to co-leads Matti Siemiatycki and Geoffrey Leonardelli. Ask for the CILA operations/accommodation lead and whether participants book individually using the Executive Programs welcome-package codes or through an employer/program block; request any existing commitments, nonlocal participant forecast and arrival/departure patterns for April 13–16, June 16–18 and October 27–29. Only after an affirmative sourcing response, propose a right-sized, nonexclusive lodging rate with a clear campus-commute proposition. Do not reserve speculative room volume or pitch replacement classroom space. Separately ask whether another cohort is planned; do not load 2028 dates without publication.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the upcoming 2027 cohort, the teaching venue is already announced at Rotman; there is no evidenced classroom-venue displacement opportunity. Lodging accessibility remains unconfirmed, not closed and not open. A nonexclusive accommodation-rate introduction may be testable, subject to whether the general Rotman hotel pathway applies and who controls it. No published evidence supports displacing an existing CILA room block.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: use 2027 to develop a university executive-education accommodation relationship and learn whether later cohorts will repeat. A future preferred-rate or module-specific lodging offer is a strategy, not an announced procurement or verified annual demand stream. No post-2027 dates, destination rotation, hotel release date or competitive rebid cycle is established.
